groups.title: Soft Capsule (D64000ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins A, B1 and B2 in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding and when physical strength is reduced during or after an illness, and for the relief of dryness of the eyes, night blindness (difficulty seeing at night), beriberi, eye fatigue, neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulder and the like), angular cheilitis (inflammation at the corners of the mouth), cheilitis (inflammation of the lips), stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth), glossitis (inflammation of the tongue), eczema and dermatitis.
groups.usage: Children aged 8 years and older and adults: take 1 capsule per dose, 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A a day may cause birth defects. Women who are within the first 3 months of pregnancy or who may be pregnant must not take it.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a baby under 3 months of age, or if you have hypersensitivity to soybean oil, soybean or peanut.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis; or if a particular risk is expected from fat overload.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. It may turn the urine yellow in urine tests and affect the results of clinical tests. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If nausea, vomiting, itching, dry and rough skin, painful swelling of the joints, loose stools, diarrhoea, loss of appetite, erythema (red patches), urticaria, eczema, rash, maculopapular rash, oedema, or oedema and fluid retention (in people with kidney failure or heart failure) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (A21500ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anaemia.
groups.usage: Children aged 12 years and older and adults: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
An overdose in a child aged 6 years or younger can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep this medicine out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have haemochromatosis (a disease in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas because of abnormal iron metabolism) or haemosiderosis; if you have anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations or antacids. Consult a pharmacist before using it together with an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If urticaria, itching, photosensitivity, abdominal or stomach pain, cramps, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever or coma occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have severe renal failure; if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to soybean oil; or if you have hypersensitivity to soybean or peanut.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are under treatment by a doctor; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. It may turn the urine yellow and may affect the results of clinical tests.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. In women taking an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, or in people with a tendency to thrombosis (blockage of a blood vessel), taking vitamin E may increase the risk of thrombosis, so take care. Taking it together with an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene may cause high blood potassium, so take care. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If diarrhoea, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, nausea, vomiting, loose stools, red patches, asystole (stopping of the heartbeat), reduced central nervous system function, or menstruation that comes earlier than expected, gradually increases in amount or lasts a long time occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for cough and sputum.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. For babies and young children aged 7 years or younger, give a syrup preparation instead. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with another antitussive-expectorant, a cold medicine, an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine) or a sedative. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals, with an interval of 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like), antitussive-expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines). Do not take this medicine if you have stopped taking an MAO inhibitor within the past 2 weeks. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. Consult a pharmacist if you have been given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema (swelling), difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness; rarely signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, reddening and burn-like blisters over the whole skin or on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes); asthma; liver function disorder (general lassitude, jaundice and the like); interstitial pneumonia (cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever); or posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance and the like).
